honestLimits: No worldwide pooled meta-analysis of dyscalculia prevalence was found (PubMed search, 2026-10-06), so the global row is a range across population studies, not one number.
Studies use different criteria and ages: figures are not directly comparable and the same data can give 1% or 6% depending on the cut-off (see england-devine-2013).
No country checked publishes an official count of dyscalculia alone. Official figures (US, England, Spain) cover broader learning-disability categories.
These are research prevalence figures, not a diagnosis of any person.

prevalence.population: School-age children, range across population studies (review)
prevalence.note: A range, not a pooled figure: no worldwide meta-analysis of dyscalculia prevalence was found.

prevalence.population: Children, adolescents and adults (German clinical guideline)
prevalence.note: The page applies the guideline range to adults as well, because dyscalculia is lifelong; no national adult estimate was found.

prevalence.population: England, one sample, depending on the criteria used
prevalence.note: The same data gave anything from 1% to 6% depending on where the line is drawn.
Reported through the Inserm collective expertise (2007), as on the site's country table.

prevalence.population: France: international studies cited by Inserm (no French study found)
prevalence.note: No French prevalence study was found; the range is from international studies in the Inserm report.
